description: /1: a worker writes a file with both declared arguments; path and bytes become facts, the limit rule sees bytes within its ceiling: ALLOW role_permits_tool + small_writes with limits.
An optional argument (bytes, required: false) may be absent: the limit rule then has no requested value and the decision is LIMIT.
FAIL CLOSED: an argument field the tool does not declare is BLOCK args_wellformed, never run.
A declared argument that is required (the default) and absent is BLOCK args_wellformed.
An argument whose value is not valid for its bound fact (path is a string; 7 is not) is BLOCK args_wellformed.
Arguments that are not an object (a bare string, as a model sometimes emits) are BLOCK args_wellformed.
A tool that declares a required argument, called with no arguments at all: BLOCK args_wellformed.
A tool with no declared arguments, called with none: ALLOW on the role check.
The same with args {}: ALLOW (an empty object carries nothing undeclared).
A tool with no declared arguments, called with one: BLOCK args_wellformed.
A fact bound to an argument may not also arrive as a fact (two sources for one value): BLOCK args_wellformed.
Arguments that are not plain JSON (a non-finite number) are BLOCK args_wellformed.
A tool the rulebook does not declare, with otherwise "deny": BLOCK unknown_tool.
A scope the rulebook does not declare: BLOCK scope_declared.
A declared tool called in a declared scope it does not list (pay in files): BLOCK scope_permits_tool.
A fact the tool requires (projected_spend, the harness's derived fact) that is absent: BLOCK required_facts — never computed, never defaulted.
A /1 request must name its principal: without principal.id it is incomplete, BLOCK required_facts.
A scope's denyRoles compile to the never rule scope_role_limits:<scope>:deny, checked before anything else: a reader in mail is BLOCK on it even though its role would also lack the tool.
The conflict check speaks /1 too: two identical write rules are a duplicate whose witness names tool, scope and principal and carries the bound argument as args; matches() must agree on it.

builtin.text: Every fact a decision needs must be supplied and valid; a missing or invalid fact is never permission.
The call's arguments are an object whose fields are exactly the tool's declared fields, each valid for its bound fact; anything else is refused, never run.
Only declared scopes are governed; a call in an undeclared scope is blocked.
Only declared roles may act; unknown roles are blocked.
A tool may be called only in the scopes it declares.
A participant may only call tools its role lists.
A tool the rulebook does not know is denied, or waits for approval, as the rulebook says (otherwise).
A delegate may call a tool only if every role in its delegation chain lists it; delegated authority never grows.
